text:
priya: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel selection change the non-chat reranker/embeddings endpoint is showing a regression in steady-state throughput and worse tail latency. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/boards/emb-rerank?q=197300
marco: ugh. numbers?
priya: baseline before change ~1.2k req/s, p95 ~120ms. after change ~900 req/s, p95 ~220ms, KV hit-rate dropped from 87% -> 62% on the same workload.
ben: do we know if kernel selection messed up the kv-cache eviction heuristic or if batching got worse (smaller batches)?
priya: initial profiler dump points at fewer multi-request kernels being chosen for short-seq models; batch formation avg size down 18%. perf-bot posted a flamegraph.
perf-bot: perf snapshot: https://perf.redwood/snapshots/1973005555
annie: can you paste the batcher configs used in the run?
priya: run config snippet:
```
batcher:
  continuous: true
  token_budget_target: 1024
  max_batch_size: 64
  window_ms: 12
  prefill_policy: early_fill
kernel_selector:
  prefer_multirequest: auto
  fallback_latency_ms: 10
kv_cache:
  shard_count: 8
  eviction: lru_timebased
```
marco: hmm early_fill + smaller window could starve multi-request kernel coalescing. Try increasing window_ms to 20 and lowering token_budget_target to 800 to allow bigger batches to form.
ben: also validate the kernel selector heuristics — the auto decision may be favoring single-request kernels for embeddings shape. Add a forced try: prefer_multirequest: prefer_if_batch>8 in canary.
priya: will run two canaries: A) revert kernel policy to previous commit, B) tune batcher to window_ms:20 + token_budget_target:800. Running now.
perf-bot: canary A deployed to ras-3 pool (ver=2026-02-18-kernelV3), canary B to ras-4 pool (ver=2026-03-01-batcher-tune)
annie: don't forget to pin quantization profile — recent kernel changed kernel path for q4_0 might affect throughput.
marco: good call. also check kv-cache locking contention metrics — if eviction storms happened it can stall batching.
ben: if kv hit rate recovered in canary A that's a strong signal kernel change impacted prefix matching or cache key layout.
priya: quick smoke results (10m): canary A throughput ~1.18k req/s, p95 125ms, kv-hit 86%. canary B throughput ~1.05k req/s, p95 150ms, kv-hit 84%.
marco: looks like kernel change was main culprit. Batcher tuning helped but didn't fully recover.
annie: action items:
- revert kernel selection policy for prod until we fix selector heuristics (marco)
- dig into kernel commit diff to see key change that touched KV key generation or cache tagging (ben)
- add a microbenchmark harness to exercise small-batch multi-request kernel paths for rerank models (priya)
- add a metric for 'multi-request kernel frequency' to console (annie)
priya: assigning. I'll open a quick PR with the workload harness and link it here.
ben: I'll start bisecting kernel commits and post findings.
marco: I'll prepare the rollback release and schedule a short maintenance window if needed.
perf-bot: perf alert cleared for rerank endpoints in prod once rollback scheduled.
priya: thanks everyone. follow-up thread with PR/links in ~2h.
marco: :thumbsup:
ben: :eyes:
annie: adding a guard in rollout policy to require kv-hit-rate >= 80% for kernel selector changes.
priya: good, that should prevent silent regressions.
